meta.topic: Critical requirement appears one day before deployment

problem:
Meridian Bank is one day from deploying an upgrade to its instant euro payment service. UAT is signed off, regression evidence is filed, the deployment window is booked and the communications to customers are ready. Late in the afternoon, the compliance team raises a requirement nobody recorded: the new service must perform Verification of Payee on instant euro payments, which is mandatory from 9 October 2025, and the current build checks the payee name only for a subset of channels. The product owner argues the gap is a new requirement that should be deferred to the next release. Compliance argues it is a mandatory obligation that cannot wait. The release manager must decide by the morning, and the wrong call either ships a non-compliant service or delays a release the business has already announced.

The decision cannot be made on opinion or on who argues loudest. It needs triage, evidence and a formal decision by the release authority. The learner must separate a defect from new scope and from a safety or compliance obligation, quantify the risk of shipping and of delaying, check whether a safe interim control exists, and present options the release authority can actually decide between. The case also carries a trap: PSD3 is sometimes cited as the source of the obligation, but PSD3 is not law and PSD2 remains in force, so the obligation must be traced to its real source, which is Regulation (EU) 2024/886 and the scheme rules, not to a directive that has not been enacted.
solution:
First classify the item precisely: is it a defect against an agreed requirement, a safety or compliance obligation, or genuinely new scope? Confirm the obligation at its source: Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025 under Regulation (EU) 2024/886, and SCT Inst execution has a 10-second maximum with no scheme-level maximum since the 2025 rulebook change. Do not cite PSD3 as the source, because PSD3 is not law and PSD2 remains in force; the provisional political agreement of 27 November 2025 does not make it applicable, with full application expected only around 2028. Then quantify the gap: which channels, payment types and volumes are affected, what happens to a payment when the check is missing, and what customer and regulatory harm follows.

Assess the options with evidence: ship as planned, ship with a safe interim control such as restricting the affected channels, delay until the check is built and tested, or deploy a hotfix with a defined regression scope. For each option record the test evidence available, the rollback position, the data migration impact, the customer communication needed and the residual risk. Present the options to the release authority with a recommendation, and record the decision, the decision maker, the evidence relied on and the follow-up actions. If the release proceeds with a known gap, that must be a formal risk acceptance by the authorised person, never an informal agreement in a meeting.

decision.question: Meridian Bank deploys an instant euro payment upgrade tomorrow. UAT is signed off. Late today, compliance raises an unrecorded requirement: Verification of Payee must apply to instant euro payments. The product owner wants to defer it; compliance says it is mandatory. You are the business analyst asked to prepare the go or no-go evidence.

options.label: A
options.detail: Add the missing Verification of Payee check overnight without testing, since the requirement is mandatory.

options.label: B
options.detail: Triage the requirement as defect, new scope or compliance obligation, quantify shipping and delaying risks, and present evidenced go or no-go options to the release authority.

options.label: C
options.detail: Ship on schedule and defer the requirement, since UAT is signed off and the release is already announced.

options.label: D
options.detail: Cancel the release permanently without a decision record, since any late requirement means the release is unsafe.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because a late requirement needs triage, evidence and a formal decision by the release authority, not a unilateral call. Option C ships a service that may breach a mandatory obligation. Option A adds an untested change to a signed-off build, which is how releases fail. Option D destroys a release that might be shippable with a safe interim control or a scoped deployment.

steps.title: Confirm the obligation, its source and its effective date
Triage the item as defect, compliance obligation or new scope
Quantify affected channels, volumes and customer harm
State what can and cannot be tested before the deployment window
Assess rollback, interim controls and deployment risk per option
Decide go, no-go or conditional go and record the decision
File decision, evidence and follow-up actions for audit

happy: The release authority makes a documented decision on evidence: either the release proceeds with a safe interim control and formal risk acceptance, or it is postponed until the check is built and tested. In both cases the decision, the decision maker, the evidence and the follow-up actions are recorded, and customers receive accurate communications about what is changing.

negative.title: Mandatory regulatory gap with no interim control
negative.detail: The missing check cannot be worked around and the obligation is already in force. Recommend postponement, record the regulatory basis and re-plan with a tested build.

negative.title: Change cannot be tested in time
negative.detail: An overnight fix has no regression evidence. Do not ship untested change; choose between delay and a scoped deployment that excludes the affected channels.

negative.title: Rollback cannot restore data
negative.detail: The deployment migrates data that cannot be reversed. Require a forward fix plan and a data backup before any go decision, and record the residual risk.

negative.title: Workaround exists but creates manual risk
negative.detail: Staff could check payee names manually for a small volume. Quantify the manual volume, error rate and staffing, and accept it only as a time-bound interim control with an expiry date.

technical: Keep the change request, the triage classification, the obligation source and effective date, the impact assessment and the release decision in one traceable record. Store test evidence with build version, environment and date so the authority can see exactly what was and was not tested. Record any risk acceptance with the name of the authorised person, the scope, the expiry and the follow-up action, and keep the customer communication version that matches the deployed scope.

messages.title: Instant credit transfer leg affected by the missing Verification of Payee check

fields.tag: Creditor name checked against the account
fields.name: Creditor name checked against the account

messages.title: Payment status report showing acceptance or rejection after the check
Customer payment initiation for the channels in scope of the check

accounting: If the release ships without the check, the bank faces payments sent to the wrong payee, customer loss, complaints and regulatory exposure, and operations would need a manual review queue with no defined capacity. If the release is delayed, the bank faces the cost of an unused deployment window, re-communication to customers and a revised launch date. Either way the accounting effect is the same discipline: no payment is released without a known status, rejected payments produce no debit, and any interim manual control must be staffed, measured and time-bound so it does not become a permanent unmonitored process.

questions.question: Who owns the go or no-go decision when a late requirement appears?
questions.explanation: The business analyst provides evidence and options; the release authority owns the go or no-go decision.

questions.question: Which statement about PSD3 is correct for this decision?
options: PSD3 only applies to direct debits
PSD3 is law and replaces PSD2
PSD3 is not law and PSD2 remains in force
questions.explanation: PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation are not law; PSD2 remains in force, with full application of the new framework expected only around 2028.

questions.question: From which date is Verification of Payee mandatory for instant euro payments?
questions.explanation: Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025.

questions.question: Why must an overnight untested fix be rejected?
options: It adds change to a signed-off build without regression evidence
questions.explanation: An untested change to a signed-off build can introduce a worse failure, and no release authority can approve it without test evidence.
